source.title: Contrastive-Difference CKA Reveals Concept-Specific Structural Alignment Across Language Model Architectures

record.file_problem: The paper text is present. Some supplementary section, table, and appendix references appear as '??', so those details are unavailable in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It measures cross-architecture concept alignment with contrastive-difference CKA and evaluates cross-model transfer, addressing representation convergence with methods different from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own alignment measurements, transfer accuracies, scale-group comparisons, and a safety SAE feature count. Statements and results attributed to prior work are not recorded as rows. Detailed supplementary pairwise results are not available in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-architecture similarity of concept representations in 4–9 LLMs using contrastive-difference CKA. It also tests learned affine maps between models. These bear on V1, V4, V5, V6 and V7 with methods unlike the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that concept representations across LLM families show moderate, concept-specific geometric convergence (CKA∆) alongside near-perfect affine-mapped functional transfer (≥94%). They call this consistent with a weak, partial form of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. They present the 70B/72B scale increase as a single-pair, hypothesis-generating observation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive-difference CKA and learned affine classifier alignment over concept-conditioned language-model activations; it does not reproduce the original study’s method. The reported large-scale evidence is observational.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment discrimination depends on the similarity measure (raw CKA versus linear or RBF CKA∆) and layer; absolute CKA∆ changes with question-set content (0.727 to 0.366 on a narrower set).

fits_no_version.finding: Within instruction-level concepts, CKA∆ rank-orders direct-transfer difficulty inversely (ρ=−1.0, n=4). It flags Gemma as an architectural outlier (d=1.08, AUC=0.79), but does not predict absolute transfer (LOO R²=−0.14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric similarity of concept representations predicts which model pairs need a learned map for transfer.

record.problems: The scale result rests on one cross-family 70B–72B pair and does not isolate scale from training-data overlap. Capability is not measured. Absolute CKA∆ is sensitive to question-set content. Safety geometric discrimination is not statistically significant (p = 0.08). Some supplementary methods and results are referenced but absent from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed model-pair, per-trait, and supplementary results are referenced in appendices but their values are not available in the supplied text. The vision-only ViT pilot is not recorded as a result for the listed versions because it is neither a scale comparison nor a vision-language paired-data test.

untested.parts: No capability measure and no controlled scale sweep within a family. The large-scale cross-family evidence is a single Llama-70B↔Qwen-72B pair.
Not tested. The ViT pilot is vision-only with no paired image-caption data.
Not tested. There are no different-seed runs of one architecture.
Stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping are not tested. Loss is measured only as binary-polarity classifier accuracy in PCA-50 space, not reconstruction.
The SAE procedure and feature identities are not given. There is no feature recurrence outside safety.
No neighbour-count sweep and no out-of-distribution inputs.
Plateau is not tested. Shared data or objectives as the cause is only raised as a confound, not tested.

missing.what: Base↔instruct pairs show CKA∆ .507 ± .089 with affine transfer .985. Fine-tuning objective shifts alignment, which a researcher would need for V7 causes.
Gemma-involving pairs have lower CKA∆ (0.696 vs 0.757 in personality; lower across all domains, d=1.08). Mistral is the code-NL outlier. Architecture dependence of convergence.
SVCCA (0.874 mean), Procrustes and mean-difference cosine baselines all show no concept discrimination (|d| ≤ 0.03; cosine d=0.007). These are further metric choices.
Cross-lingual gradient: CKA∆ is 0.812 for French and 0.593 for Chinese, possibly confounded with training data. This is input dependence.
Same-family cross-scale values: Llama-70B↔Llama-8B 0.905 and Qwen-72B↔Qwen-7B 0.819, both above the cross-family values.

record.verdict_notes: Direct-transfer rows are baselines, so they cannot limit V4, which allows a learned map. The record's V4 limits_scope label built on them is withdrawn. Affine rows are unlinked from V7: near-perfect functional transfer coexists with partial geometric alignment, and V7 concerns representational alignment. The V1 evidence is weak: the small-model group differs in family, the paper attributes its drop to diversity, and large-scale evidence is one pair confounded with data overlap. This is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The claimed joint trend with model capability is not directly tested: no capability measure or controlled scale sweep is reported. The large-scale comparison is one cross-family 70B–72B pair.
No vision-language comparison on paired images and captions. A vision-only ViT pilot is not a cross-modal vision-language test.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations of the same architecture.

Tests learned affine alignment of classifier representations. It does not test stitching, relative representations, maps without paired data, or whether the map is universally low-loss outside the reported concept tasks.
The reported universal-versus-architecture-specific feature counts are for safety; the supplied text does not give feature-level interpretability or recurrence results for other domains.
Tests linear versus RBF CKA, raw versus contrastive-difference CKA, and reports prompt-set sensitivity. It does not systematically sweep the number of neighbours or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports partial geometric alignment and notes possible training-data-overlap confounding, but does not isolate shared training data or objectives as the cause, nor test a plateau.
